catalog_quote: [p.50] The accentual systems of all other Bs dialects have phonetic details involving both vowel length and stress. The vowel in an accented open penult (CV) is long: all dialects (but Kuy and Tsg) bataq ~ ba:taq young. The vowel in an unaccented (CV) or closed (CVC) syllable is short: all dialects manuk ~ manuk chicken. Except for cases of compensatory lengthening, the vowel in the ultima is short ... In all dialects studied (except Kuy) stems or derivatives with a closed penult [CVC.CV(C)] are accented on the penult (see 10.2.1.). new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent (realised as vowel length plus stress on an open penult, stress alone elsewhere) is phonemic and lexically contrastive between penult and ultima in Northern Sorsogon as in all Bisayan varieties other than some Kuyonon/Tausug dialects; it is predictable only when the penult is closed (then penult-stressed). Sorsogon, with Masbate and the Waray group, additionally allows inherited length in the antepenult (e.g. in verb prefixes).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated as such; antepenultimate (prefixal) vowel length is said to occur freely in Masbate, Sorsogon and Waray-area dialects (p.216, p.245).
new_statements.exceptions: Closed penult is always stressed regardless of base accent (8.10.2); stress placement can be overridden by exclamatory intonation while length stays (3.1.3, p.50-51); accent shifts with certain affixes (4.2); Kuyonon and Jolo Tausug have lost the contrast (not relevant to Sor).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonemic accent on citation forms; Zorc adds that 'in all dialects stress is a syntactic feature, a means of counting the full words in a clause' and that stress (not length) may shift under sentence intonation. Statement is a cross-Bisayan generalisation in a comparative-historical monograph; Sor is covered as one of the 36 dialects, with its data taken from McFarland 1974.
new_statements.identity_note: Zorc 1977 treats this language under the abbreviation 'Sor' = 'Sorsogon, Northern Sorsogon' (surusugunun, Table 2 no. 33, Central Bisayan, Peripheral group with Mas), i.e. Masbate Sorsogon [bks] masb1237, distinct from 'Gub' = Gubat/Southern Sorsogon (= Waray Sorsogon, sout2918?) and 'Mas' = Masbatenyo (masb1238). Zorc's Sor data were drawn from McFarland 1974, not his own fieldwork ('DATA SOURCE: McFarland'). Lobel 2013 calls the same language 'Central Sorsoganon'. The accent statements quoted are generalisations over 'all Bs dialects (except Kuy and Tsg)', in which Sor is included and is named explicitly only in the exception lists concerning antepenultimate length (pp.216, 245).
